Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name. There will be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud's results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year 2024. With me on the call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Product Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud delivered another strong fourth quarter, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

I'm thrilled to kick off our financial highlights today, as we delivered another standout quarter that underscores our leadership in the cloud computing landscape. We significantly exceeded our guidance across key metrics, driven by accelerating demand for AI workloads, resilient enterprise consumption, and the early payoffs from our strategic investments in next-generation infrastructure.

Let me start with the top line. Total revenue reached $28.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter, smashing our guidance midpoint by $1.2 billion. This marks our 15th straight quarter of at least 15% YoY growth, outpacing the broader cloud market as tracked by Synergy Research, where hyperscaler growth averaged around 14% in the quarter. Cloud services revenue – our core engine – hit $26.1 billion, representing 92% of total revenue and growing 20% YoY. Within cloud, infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) surged 25% YoY to $18.2 billion, fueled by a 52% explosion in AI/ML compute workloads, as customers ramped up GPU-intensive training and inference on our Nexara AI Foundry platform.

Platform-as-a-service (PaaS) revenue climbed 16% YoY to $5.4 billion, bolstered by adoption of our serverless Kubernetes services and data analytics tools, which saw a 30% uptick in containerized workloads. Storage and databases grew steadily at 12% YoY to $2.5 billion, with object storage margins benefiting from our shift to next-gen tape archival solutions for cost-sensitive archival use cases.

Customer metrics remain a bright spot, reflecting sticky expansion in our base. Annualized run-rate (ARR) crossed $105 billion, up 22% YoY, while remaining performance obligations (RPO) stood at $165 billion, up 28% YoY – our strongest RPO growth in two years, signaling robust multi-year commitments amid economic uncertainty. Net revenue retention (NRR) held strong at 112%, with expansion in our top 500 customers averaging 128% – driven by 85 customers surpassing $100 million in annual spend, including several Fortune 50 migrations from legacy on-prem VMware environments.

On profitability, we continue to expand margins through operational leverage and efficiency gains. GAAP gross margin expanded 210 basis points YoY to 78.2%, our highest in five quarters, thanks to optimized data center utilization hitting 85% globally and the ramp of our proprietary Nexara Graviton4 Arm-based instances, which deliver 40% better price-performance than comparable x86 alternatives. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 32.5%, up from 30.8% a year ago, as we kept sales and marketing at 18% of revenue despite heavy AI go-to-market investments. Operating income came in at $9.3 billion, and free cash flow generated a robust $10.2 billion, or 36% of revenue, giving us ample dry powder for our capex plan this fiscal year, skewed toward AI data center builds.

Regionally, performance was balanced yet differentiated. The Americas drove 55% of revenue at $15.7 billion, up 21% YoY, anchored by U.S. public sector wins including a $2.5 billion multi-year deal with a leading defense contractor for sovereign AI workloads. EMEA contributed 25% or $7.1 billion, growing 17% YoY despite macro headwinds in Germany and the UK, where our Frankfurt and London regions saw double-digit compute growth from financial services firms adopting our FedRAMP High-equivalent controls. APAC was the star, delivering 20% of revenue at $5.7 billion and +19% YoY growth, led by Japan and India expansions – our Tokyo region now powers over 40% of the country's public cloud AI inference.

Strategically, these results validate our 'AI-First Cloud' thesis. We've deployed over 1 million Nexara Nitro GPUs – our custom HBM3e-accelerated chips co-engineered akin to Nvidia's H100 ecosystem – capturing 15% market share in public cloud AI training per Gartner estimates. Technical initiatives like our Zero-Trust Edge Mesh for 5G/edge computing reduced latency by 60% for telco partners, driving 35% YoY growth in edge services. Sustainability efforts are paying off too: our data centers now run on 75% renewable energy, ahead of our 2030 net-zero pledge.

Now I'll turn the call over to Michael Patel to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. We are pleased with our financial results for the fourth quarter. Revenue increased by 18% year-over-year to $28.5 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 78.2%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 32.5%.

Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our capital expenditure outlook and investment plans, which remain a cornerstone of our strategy to capture the explosive growth in cloud computing demand, particularly driven by generative AI, machine learning workloads, and enterprise digital transformation.

For the full year 2024, we delivered on our Capex guidance with total spend of $28.2 billion, up 22% year-over-year from $23.1 billion in 2023. This included $18.7 billion—or 66% of total Capex—allocated to data center capacity expansion and refresh, $5.4 billion to compute and storage infrastructure, including next-gen accelerators, and $4.1 billion to networking, edge facilities, and R&D prototypes. In Q4 alone, we deployed $7.8 billion, reflecting accelerated timelines to meet surging demand from hyperscale customers mirroring large-scale inference needs.

Looking ahead to fiscal 2025, we are guiding for Capex in the range of $32 billion to $36 billion, representing 14-28% growth over 2024. This step-up is deliberate and disciplined, funded entirely from operations with no dilution to our path toward $15 billion in free cash flow this year. Let me break this down by key investment pillars.

Data center expansion will account for 70% of 2025 Capex, approximately $23-25 billion. The AI boom has compressed our supply timelines—global demand for high-density GPU clusters is outpacing forecasts, with AI-related workloads now comprising 42% of new bookings, up from 28% a year ago. We're prioritizing hyperscale builds with 1GW+ campuses, incorporating liquid immersion cooling to achieve PUEs below 1.15, a 20% efficiency gain over air-cooled predecessors. Key initiatives include North America taking 45% of DC Capex with 2.5 million square feet across Virginia, Oregon, and new sites in Texas and Ohio, housing over 50,000 NVIDIA H200 and Blackwell GPUs by mid-2025. EMEA gets 25%, with sovereign cloud ramps in Frankfurt, Paris, and a new 500MW facility in Milan to comply with EU Data Act and GDPR. APAC and emerging markets take 30%, with $4 billion to Singapore, Tokyo, Mumbai, and a 300MW data center in Riyadh tapping Saudi Vision 2030.

We're on track for 25% annualized capacity growth, ensuring under 2ms intra-region latency for AI inference at scale.

Compute and storage innovations represent 15% of Capex, about $5-6 billion. Beyond NVIDIA silicon, we're advancing custom ASICs—our second-gen Nexara Inference Engine (NIE-2), delivering 3x better TOPS per watt for transformer models. We'll deploy over 100,000 NIE-2 units in 2025, targeting 15-20% reduction in customer TCO for fine-tuning. Storage focuses on QLC NAND and disaggregated architectures, boosting exabyte-scale object storage durability to 11 9's while cutting costs 30% via Nexara Glacier Deep Archive.

Networking, edge, and sustainability get 10%, around $3-4 billion. For 400Gbps+ Ethernet fabrics, we're investing in silicon photonics switches. Edge computing receives $1.2 billion for 50 new micro-data centers in 5G corridors, enabling telco partnerships. All new builds are PUE-optimized with 100% renewable sourcing via PPAs, targeting carbon neutrality by 2028, and hydro-powered sites in Quebec and Norway.

R&D and efficiency levers take 5%, $1.5-2 billion, funding software-defined infrastructure like AutoScaler ML for 18% CapEx efficiency gains, and quantum-safe cryptography pilots.

This Capex profile reflects a multi-year ROI of 3-4x on AI infrastructure, with payback periods compressing to 18 months. Our supply chain diversification—40% non-NVIDIA compute by 2026—de-risks execution. We expect CapEx intensity to peak at 12-14% of revenue in 2025 before tapering to 10% by 2027 as utilization exceeds 85%.

These investments fortify our market position, with 28% cloud market share growth in AI services. Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation Nexara Compute platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q4 FY2024 earnings call. I'm thrilled to dive into one of our most critical metrics: Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO. RPO represents the aggregated amount of revenue we have contracted with customers but have not yet recognized. It's our North Star for revenue visibility in the cloud computing industry, providing a clear view into future performance amid multi-year, subscription-based contracts.

In the cloud sector, RPO captures committed spend on IaaS, PaaS, and high-margin SaaS like Nexara AI Studio and Nexara Edge Orchestrator. It reflects sticky revenue from data gravity, AI model training, and hybrid/multi-cloud setups.

For Q4, total RPO reached $165 billion, up 28% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter. This outpaces the public cloud market's 22% growth per Gartner. Current RPO—within 12 months—stood at around $66 billion, up 25% YoY, equating to about 40% of total and 2.2x our quarterly revenue. Non-current RPO surged to $99 billion, up 30% YoY and 60% of total, driven by longer contracts averaging 36 months for AI infrastructure and sovereign cloud.

Our dollar-based net expansion rate held at 118%, with 65% of bookings from existing customer upsell, especially 2-3x expansions in AI/ML.

Drivers include AI tailwinds: Nexara AI Platform drove 45% of new RPO, with hyperscale demand for RAG pipelines adding commitments like $500 million over three years. AI-related RPO now at roughly $45 billion, 27% of backlog.

Multi-cloud momentum via Nexara Interconnect added $12 billion to non-current RPO, including $1.2 billion from a European automotive OEM for edge-to-cloud inference.

Strategic verticals like healthcare and financial services contributed 32%, with Snowflake partnerships adding $800 million.

Regionally: Americas 55% at $90.8 billion, up 24% YoY with federal deals; EMEA 25% at $41.3 billion, up 35% on sovereign cloud; APAC 20% at $33 billion, up 32% led by Japan and India.

RPO provides visibility into FY2025, projecting over $200 billion by year-end. We're investing Capex toward AI infrastructure like 20,000 H200s, sustainability for 100% renewables by 2026, and Nexara Agents Framework for workflow autonomy.

Risks like currency headwinds are derisked by 60% non-current weighting. Our growth outstrips peers.

This positions us for 25%+ top-line growth through the AI megacycle. Now, I'll pass it over to Jordan Lee for a product roadmap update.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Elena. We are excited about the market reception to our new Nexara AI Foundry offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the enterprise AI sector.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our Cloud services gross margin performance, which came in at 78.2% for the quarter, up 450 basis points year-over-year and 120 basis points sequentially. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of expansion, driven by operational efficiencies, product mix shifts, and hyperscale tailwinds.

Revenue mix dynamics contributed 280 basis points, with compute and AI/ML at 58% of Cloud revenue, up from 49% YoY. High-margin AI services like Nexara Confidential Compute exceed 82% margins versus storage at 62-65%. AI Hypercluster adoption surged 140% QoQ.

Infrastructure efficiencies added 110 basis points, with 87% server utilization via Nexara Fleet Manager and custom Silicon Engine ASICs delivering 25% better efficiency. PUE improved to 1.18 through liquid cooling and 75% renewables.

Depreciation stabilized at 24.5% of revenue, with in-house sourcing shaving 15% off capex. Bandwidth costs held despite 35% traffic growth.

Regionally: North America at 76.5% with 92% utilization; EMEA 74.2% on sovereign wins; APAC 68.9% ramping newer markets; LatAm 65.2% improving via partnerships.

We mitigated capex rises and competition with 98.5% SLAs and pricing power. Bets like Nexara Quantum Networking target further uplifts.

We guide Q1 Cloud gross margin to 78.5-79.0%, positioning us ahead of industry averages. I'll now hand it over to Taylor Kim to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before diving deeper, I want to address the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations on our reported results. As a global cloud provider with over 55% of revenue from outside the U.S., we're exposed to currency volatility like our peers.

In Q4, the strengthening USD reduced reported revenue by $285 million, or 3.5 percentage points, versus constant currency. YoY, FX shaved 210 basis points off growth, with constant currency at 30%.

Regionally: EMEA ($2.5B, 30%) faced euro 8% depreciation ($120M hit), but 35% constant growth; APAC ($2B, 25%) yen/AUD weakness ($95M), 25% constant; LatAm ($650M) BRL 7% drop ($45M).

Trailing twelve months, FX reduced $780M. Usage-based revenue is sensitive, but ARR offers stability.

Mitigations include 70% hedging for Q1, localized pricing at 85% of contracts, regional capacity in strengthening currencies, USD/hedged RPO at 65%, and multi-cloud fabric.

We expect Q1 FX 2-3 point headwind, but constant currency underscores momentum. Back to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Taylor. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Thank you, everyone. I'll now turn to our outlook for the first quarter and full fiscal year 2025, focusing on our Cloud segment, 82% of revenue this year.

For Q1 FY2025 Cloud revenue, we expect $12.4 billion to $12.6 billion, 18-20% YoY growth. AI/ML over 50% QoQ, storage mid-teens, IaaS/PaaS sustaining. Americas 19%, EMEA 22%, APAC 25%+.

RPO at $185 billion supports this.

Full FY2025 Cloud: $52.5-53.5 billion, 24-26% growth.

Full company: Q1 total $15.1-15.3 billion, 17-19% YoY; FY2025 $64.0-65.5 billion, 22-25% growth, op margins 32-33%.

Guidance assumes stable FX, GPU normalization. AI tailwinds offset macro.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks for taking my question, and congrats on a great quarter. Sarah, can you elaborate on the sustainability of AI demand and how it's shaping your long-term capex allocation, especially with peers facing GPU constraints?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Ben. AI demand remains robust, with workloads now 42% of bookings and growing. Our capex ramp to $32-36 billion in FY2025 prioritizes GPU clusters and custom ASICs like NIE-2 to meet this, with diversification de-risking supply. Utilization at 85%+ ensures quick ROI, positioning us strongly in the $1 trillion cloud economy.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Great results, team. Michael, on the revenue guidance, how are you factoring in ongoing FX volatility and potential macro slowdowns into the FY2025 outlook?

Michael Patel:
Thanks, Lisa. Our guidance is on a constant currency basis, baking in a 2-3 point FX headwind similar to Q4. With RPO visibility at $185 billion and AI driving 50%+ QoQ growth in key segments, we're confident even if non-AI softens slightly. Hedging covers 70% of exposure, and Cloud mix expansion supports margin gains to 32-33%.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
